questions.question: What did people historically believe about the shape of the Earth and the movement of heavenly bodies?
options: Earth was flat, with the Sun and stars moving around it
Earth was a sphere orbiting around the Sun
Earth was flat, but remained completely motionless while stars stood still
Earth was a cube surrounded by water and orbiting the Moon

questions.question: Up until the 16th century, what was the most widely accepted belief regarding Earth's position in the universe?
options: The Sun was located at the very centre of the universe
Earth was located at the centre of the universe
The Moon was at the centre, surrounded by all planets
Earth was at the outer edge of an expanding galaxy

questions.question: Which scientific tool provided crucial observational evidence that helped us better understand the universe?
options: Barometers
Microscopes
Telescopes
Seismometers

questions.question: At what angle is the axis of Earth's spin tilted?
options: 0 degrees
12.5 degrees
23.5 degrees
45 degrees

questions.question: In which direction does the gravitational force of a planet or star pull objects?
options: Away from its outer atmosphere
Towards the centre of the planet or star
In a sideways tangent to its surface
Towards the nearest neighboring star

questions.question: How does the mass of an object affect the strength of its gravity?
options: The greater the mass, the stronger its gravity
The greater the mass, the weaker its gravity
Mass has no effect on the strength of gravity
Gravity only exists if an object has no mass

questions.question: What happens to the gravitational force of a planet as an object moves further away from it into space?
options: It gets stronger
It gets weaker
It disappears instantly
It remains completely constant

questions.question: How does Earth's gravity affect the motion of the Moon?
options: It causes the Moon to stop moving completely
It pushes the Moon further out into space
It speeds up the Moon's spin until it breaks apart
It pulls the Moon towards Earth's centre, changing its direction into an orbit

questions.question: Why does Earth follow an orbit around the Sun rather than traveling in a straight line?
options: Earth is pushed along by solar wind
The Sun's gravity pulls Earth towards its centre, changing Earth's direction
The magnetic field of the Moon pulls Earth around the Sun
Earth's atmosphere propels it around the Sun

questions.question: How does the spreading of light rays compare when light hits a surface face-on versus at an angle?
options: Light rays are less spread out when hitting face-on
Light rays are more spread out when hitting face-on
Light rays spread out equally at all angles
Light rays only spread out when hitting at an angle of zero degrees

questions.question: At what time of day is the heating effect of the Sun greatest at a location on Earth?
options: Sunrise
Midday
Sunset
Midnight

questions.question: Which statement best defines a planet?
options: A very large sphere of rock or gas that orbits a star
An extremely hot sphere of gas that gives out light
A small chunk of ice that travels outside the solar system
A glowing cloud of dust floating between galaxies

questions.question: Besides the 8 planets, which objects orbit the Sun in our solar system?
options: Galaxies and black holes
Dwarf planets and smaller objects such as asteroids
Other major stars and nebulae
Comets made purely of glowing hot gas like the Sun

questions.question: What happens in the northern and southern hemispheres during the month of December?
options: Northern hemisphere has summer; southern hemisphere has winter
Northern hemisphere has winter; southern hemisphere has summer
Both hemispheres experience summer simultaneously
Both hemispheres experience winter simultaneously

questions.question: Why do countries located near the Equator not experience typical summer and winter seasons?
options: They receive no direct sunlight during any month
Their axis of rotation flips every six months
They stay close to 'face-on' to the Sun all year round
They are tilted completely away from the Sun all year

questions.question: Why do stars in the night sky appear so much smaller and dimmer than our Sun?
options: They are much cooler than the Sun
They are much further away from Earth than the Sun is
They do not emit their own light
They are blocked by Earth's thick atmosphere

questions.question: What is a light-year?
options: The time it takes for Earth to orbit the Sun once
The distance light travels in one year
The time it takes light from the Sun to reach Earth
The brightness of a star measured over one year

questions.question: What is a galaxy?
options: A single solar system containing one planet
A group containing billions of stars in the universe
A collection of eight planets orbiting a moon
A belt of asteroids floating between two stars

questions.question: Which everyday event is explained by Earth spinning on its axis?
options: The occurrence of day and night
The change of ocean tides
The orbit of the Moon around Earth
The change of the calendar year

questions.question: The Moon orbits Earth approximately once every 27.3 days. What does this orbital motion explain?
options: Why the Moon appears to change shape over time
Why Earth experiences leap years
Why the Sun appears to rise in the west
Why Earth's axis angle changes over time
